history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - it is a royal memorial pavilion, not a place of worship; keep-or-drop decision needed. Ganga Deri is a white-marble memorial on the banks of Gangajaliya Talao in central Bhavnagar, built by Maharaja Takhtsinhji of Bhavnagar in memory of his wife Maharani Majirajba (Rajba), who died in 1875 while giving birth to the heir Bhavsinhji II. It was designed by Sir John Griffith, principal of the J.J. School of Art, Bombay; one detailed source gives construction 1877-1893 (finished 1893), while trawell.in and threebestrated.in print '1983' - almost certainly a typo for 1883/1893 (verify). The two-storey edifice is a Mughal-Rajput / Indo-Saracenic synthesis often called a 'mini Taj Mahal', with a chhatri, pavilion, bridge, delicately carved floral jaalis (lattice screens) and columns; the state insignia with the motto 'Man Proposes, but God Disposes' is displayed. It stands ~1 km from Bhavnagar railway station and is free to visit.

town_description: Bhavnagar is a port city on the Gulf of Cambay in Saurashtra, Gujarat, and was the capital of the former Bhavnagar princely state founded in 1723 by Bhavsinhji Gohil.
